S01.meta: // SLIDE 01 — HOOK: same drug trial, two ways to read the result — surrogate endpoints vs hard endpoints

branches.label: Surrogate endpoints
branches.detail: ORR 60% vs 20% — tumors shrank three times as often. PFS improved. Drug is biologically active.
branches.fix: What the drug does to the tumor.

branches.label: Hard endpoints
branches.detail: Overall survival: curves nearly identical. Grade 3–4 toxicity: higher on new drug. Patients did not live longer and felt worse.
branches.fix: What the drug does for the patient.

resolver.label: It depends entirely on what 'work' means
resolver.detail: The gap between what a treatment does to the tumor and what it does for the patient is the subject of this chapter.

S06.meta: // SLIDE 06 — ENDPOINT HIERARCHY: three-tier validity ladder from fast proxies to hard truth

modes.label: Overall Response Rate · Biomarker
modes.sub: fastest proxies — tumor shrinkage, PSA, CA-125, ctDNA
modes.limit: a hypothesis about benefit, not benefit itself
modes.resolves: must be validated before standing in for survival

modes.label: Progression-Free Survival
modes.sub: surrogate — valid only when validated in this specific cancer type
modes.limit: earns the right to stand in — where formal validation exists

modes.label: Overall Survival · Quality of Life
modes.sub: hard endpoints — what patients care about; years to mature in trials
modes.limit: the arbiters — no surrogate overrules these
modes.resolves: the final word on whether a treatment benefits patients

data.axisLabel: Endpoint validity — proxy to hard truth

S08.meta: // SLIDE 08 — READING THE OPENING CASE: apply the hierarchy — surrogates look good, hard endpoints flat or worse

data.axisLabel: Result for new drug vs old

items.label: Grade 3–4 toxicity — higher on new drug (hard endpoint, wrong direction)

S10.meta: // SLIDE 10 — PSEUDOPROGRESSION: same scan signal, two interpretations — RECIST says stop, iRECIST says wait

data.startLabel: First post-immunotherapy scan: tumor lesions appear larger
data.splitLabel: Is this true progression or immune infiltration?

tracks.label: Standard RECIST
tracks.outcome: Progressive disease declared → drug discontinued → working treatment abandoned
notes: Tumor enlargement classified as non-response at first timepoint
Immune cells infiltrating tumor caused transient inflammation — not true progression

tracks.label: iRECIST — confirm at second timepoint
tracks.outcome: Apparent progression confirmed or denied → if immune response, tumor regresses
notes: Modified criteria require a confirmatory scan before declaring failure
Immune response has time to declare itself
Protects patients from losing a treatment that is actually working
